sub_indicators.label: Government hosting and cloud policy
sub_indicators.subject: gov.policy
sub_indicators.text: Data storage / cloud strategy: hosting policy
sub_indicators.norm_short: The African Union's Data Policy Framework asks each state to set rules for hosting its own data, by category, and to build national or regional cloud capacity. Its Digital Transformation Strategy sets a target for hosting the continent's content on the continent.
criteria: A source from the past three years says the government has no hosting or cloud policy and none is being written.

A government hosting or cloud policy is being written or is out for consultation, or the last one has ended with no successor adopted. A data centre or government cloud with no policy behind it does not count.

A policy on where the state's data is hosted, or on how public bodies may use cloud, is adopted and in force. It may be a cloud-first policy, a circular, a hosting standard or part of a larger strategy or law. Where public bodies must host is not yet named.
The government has named where public bodies must host: a government cloud or data centre in service that the policy tells them to use, or a published list of approved providers.
Public bodies have moved onto the named hosting in the past three years: a dated source names or counts the ministries or agencies that have. How good the policy is, is not judged.
